strategies.latest_batch: naive retraining from the latest released batch; one-class batches are skipped because the binary learner cannot be fitted
strategies.rolling_replay: retraining from released feedback plus a bounded rolling history

label_delay_semantics: labels from batch t are released after predictions for batch t+d and can first affect batch t+d+1

parameters.sampling: deterministic systematic temporal sample spanning each complete day

monday.ordering: microsecond Unix timestamp with documented LYCOS tie-breakers; deterministic systematic temporal sample across the complete day

tuesday.ordering: microsecond Unix timestamp with documented LYCOS tie-breakers; deterministic systematic temporal sample across the complete day

wednesday.ordering: microsecond Unix timestamp with documented LYCOS tie-breakers; deterministic systematic temporal sample across the complete day

thursday.ordering: microsecond Unix timestamp with documented LYCOS tie-breakers; deterministic systematic temporal sample across the complete day

friday.ordering: microsecond Unix timestamp with documented LYCOS tie-breakers; deterministic systematic temporal sample across the complete day

limitations: The experiment uses one natural capture-day order and does not claim order robustness.
Label availability is simulated as trusted supervision after a configurable delay.
Algorithmic configurations quantify learner stability, not population replications.
The systematic pilot sample thins the stream when max_events_per_day is set.
This evaluates binary intrusion detection; family labels are used only for retention analysis.
